writing.prompt: Directions: Suppose your university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on future applications of robots on campus. You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but not more than 180 words.
writing.sample: Robots are no longer figures from science fiction; in the near future, they are likely to become common helpers on university campuses. As the university newspaper invites students to imagine future applications of robots on campus, I believe intelligent machines will mainly reshape our campus life in three areas: library services, laboratory assistance, and daily guidance.First, in the library, robots could locate, fetch, and even deliver requested books to reading rooms, saving students valuable study time. Second, in science labs, robotic assistants might handle repetitive experiments or dangerous chemicals, allowing students to focus on analysis and innovation. Third, robots placed around the campus could provide real-time directions and campus information for visitors and freshmen, reducing confusion during busy periods.Of course, these technologies should serve people rather than replace human interaction. If universities introduce robots wisely, campus life will become more efficient, safe, and welcoming.

transcript.en: A 104-year-old woman is selling the house she has lived in since she was two years old. Nancy Gifford was born months after the end of the First World War, and spent 102 years living in her three-bedroom house in the Somerset Village of Street. She is now putting it on the market, having lived in it through the Second World War and the invention of television.
transcript.zh: 一名104岁的女子正在出售她从两岁起就一直居住的房子。南希·吉福德出生于第一次世界大战结束几个月后，在萨默塞特郡斯特里特村的这栋三居室房屋中生活了102年。如今，她准备将房子挂牌出售；她曾在这里度过第二次世界大战时期，也见证了电视的发明。

transcript.en: Her family bought the house for £200 in 1921. And it is now priced at some £170,000. According to the Bank of England's inflation calculator, £200 in 1921 would be worth £7,750 today. According to the estate agent, the house was built in 1882 and originally featured a well for the entire road. Except for some changes in the toilet and wash area, much of the house remains the same. Mrs. Gifford is selling the house and moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury because of her health.
transcript.zh: 她的家人于1921年以200英镑买下了这栋房子，而如今房子的售价约为17万英镑。根据英格兰银行的通货膨胀计算器，1921年的200英镑相当于如今的7750英镑。据房地产经纪人介绍，这栋房子建于1882年，最初设有一口供整条街使用的水井。除厕所和盥洗区有所改动外，房屋的大部分仍保持原样。由于健康原因，吉福德夫人正在出售房子，并搬到附近格拉斯顿伯里的养老院。

transcript.en: The navy rescued a man who survived 24 days floating in the sea on a boat by eating tomato sauce and vegetable powder. The man, 47, wrote the word "HELP" in English on the boat, which was key to his rescue.
transcript.zh: 海军救起了一名男子，他靠食用番茄酱和蔬菜粉，在一艘船上漂浮海上生存了24天。这名47岁的男子在船上用英语写下了“HELP”一词，这对他的获救起到了关键作用。

transcript.en: The man told authorities that his experience began in December when currents swept the sailboat out to sea while he was making repairs. To survive, the man collected rainwater with a cloth. He had to constantly remove water from the boat to prevent it from sinking. He also tried to light a fire to send a distress signal without success. Finally, a plane passed by and he signaled with a mirror. He said the navy told him that he was spotted when the plane passed again. The sailboat was abandoned at sea when the man was picked up by a nearby merchant ship. He was found in good health but had lost weight.
transcript.zh: 这名男子告诉当局，他的遭遇始于12月，当时他正在维修帆船，洋流将帆船冲向了大海。为了生存，他用一块布收集雨水。他不得不不断将船里的水排出去，以防船只沉没。他还试图生火发出求救信号，但没有成功。最后，一架飞机经过时，他用镜子发出了信号。他说，海军告诉他，飞机再次经过时发现了他。这名男子被附近的一艘商船救起时，帆船已被遗弃在海上。他被发现时身体状况良好，但体重有所下降。

transcript.zh: 丹佛公立学校董事会将关闭数所小学和初中，以弥补因入学人数下降而减少的预算。学区发言人表示，具体关闭的学校将在未来几天内公布。

transcript.en: The school board approved criteria to close schools with fewer than 215 students, as well as schools with fewer than 275 students and a projected decline in enrollment. In the next three years, the district expects to enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students, it said. "3,000 students may not seem like that many students, but to a budget where you're receiving per-pupil funding, that's about 36 million dollars," district spokesperson Scott Pribble said. "We know that there are impacts and it's heartbreaking and difficult work. But in order for the district to stay out of debt, it's a step that needs to be taken," he said. The district said the decreased budget means it cannot provide the same mental health supports, social and emotional services or specialized programming to schools with lower enrollment.
transcript.zh: 学校董事会批准了关闭学校的标准：学生人数少于215人的学校，以及学生人数少于275人且预计入学人数还会下降的学校。学区表示，未来三年，预计小学和初中的学生人数将减少3,000人。学区发言人斯科特·普里布尔说：“3,000名学生可能看起来并不算多，但对于一个按照学生人数获得拨款的预算来说，这大约意味着3,600万美元。”他说：“我们知道这会带来影响，这项工作令人心碎，也十分艰难。但为了让学区避免陷入债务，这是必须采取的一步。”学区表示，预算减少意味着无法再为入学人数较少的学校提供同等水平的心理健康支持、社会与情感服务或专业课程。

transcript.en: M: That's OK, madam. I can book it and take the payment over the phone if that's not a problem for you.
transcript.zh: M: 没关系，女士。如果您不介意的话，我可以帮您预订，并通过电话收取票款。

transcript.en: W: That would be wonderful. I'm not very good with computers. My husband usually does all of these things, but he is in Italy on a business trip until next Thursday, and I know how quickly these things can sell out.
transcript.zh: W: 那太好了。我不太会用电脑。这些事情通常都是我丈夫处理的，但他要到下周四才结束在意大利的出差，而我知道这些票很快就会售罄。

transcript.zh: W: 是的，就是那场。我需要两张票，谢谢，位置不要离前排太近。

transcript.zh: M: 实际上，前排的票已经全部售罄了。不过我可以给您安排楼上的两张票，位置靠近中间。我想您应该不想坐得太高吧。

transcript.zh: M: 没问题，女士。我现在就为您预留那两个座位，之后我们只需要您的卡号和全名，办完这些就可以了。

transcript.en: If U.S. workers want to switch jobs, they'd better do it now. Last year, job switchers earned far higher wage increases than those staying in their jobs. But the gap is now closing. A three-month moving average of annual wage increases from the Atlanta Federal Reserve Bank's Wage Tracker shows that U.S. job switchers got the highest wage increase last July, when the measure touched 8.5%. Since then, it has gone up and down, and has been going steadily down since November. The gap in wage gains between people who switched jobs and those who stayed in their jobs is now closing. On average, people who changed jobs have almost always gotten better pay raises than those who stayed. But in the past, the difference was usually around one percentage point. In July though, the gap widened to 2.6 percentage points.
transcript.zh: 如果美国工人想换工作，最好现在就行动。去年，跳槽者的工资涨幅远高于留在原岗位的人。但如今这一差距正在缩小。亚特兰大联邦储备银行工资追踪器显示，美国跳槽者年度工资涨幅的三个月移动平均值在去年7月达到最高，当时触及8.5%。此后，该指标有所起伏，并自11月以来持续下降。跳槽者与留在原岗位者之间的工资涨幅差距如今正在缩小。平均而言，换过工作的人几乎总是比留在原岗位的人获得更高的加薪幅度。但过去两者之间的差距通常约为一个百分点，而在7月，这一差距扩大到了2.6个百分点。

transcript.en: But now wage growth is slowing down for everyone, and job switchers are getting smaller wage bumps in their new jobs. At the moment, those who change jobs get an average 7.3% raise every year, while those who stay get a 5.4% raise. That suggests the demand for workers has reached, or is at least nearing, its peak. The labor market is likely cooling, because even a shortage of workers isn't overcoming the historic imbalance between employers and employees in the U.S. The volume of income that workers take home as a proportion of what the U.S. economy produces is still falling.
transcript.zh: 但现在每个人的工资增速都在放缓，跳槽者在新工作中获得的加薪幅度也越来越小。目前，换工作的人平均每年加薪7.3%，而留在原岗位的人加薪5.4%。这表明，对工人的需求已经达到或至少接近峰值。劳动力市场可能正在降温，因为即使存在工人短缺，也无法克服美国雇主与雇员之间历史性的失衡。工人带回家的收入总额占美国经济产出的比例仍在下降。

transcript.en: Highly processed foods—the kinds made with lots of sugar, fat and salt—make up as much as 60% of the average American diet. But a new study shows that their low price and convenience come at a cost to health. The study found that when people ate a highly processed diet, they consumed about 500 more calories per day than they did when they ate a less processed diet. They also gained two pounds over two weeks, even though both diets had the same amounts of nutrients, like sugar, fat, fiber and salt.
transcript.zh: 高度加工食品，即含有大量糖、脂肪和盐的食品，占美国人平均饮食的比例高达60%。但一项新的研究表明，这类食品低廉的价格和便利性是以健康为代价的。研究发现，人们食用高度加工的饮食时，每天摄入的热量比食用加工程度较低的饮食时多约500卡路里。尽管两种饮食所含的营养成分，如糖、脂肪、纤维和盐，数量相同，他们在两周内仍增重了两磅。

transcript.en: It wasn't a shock to find highly processed foods weren't healthy; other research has linked them to a higher risk of cancer and obesity. What was unexpected was that sugar, fat and salt didn't seem to be what caused people to overeat. This is the first trial that demonstrates that there is something about highly processed foods—independent of those nutrients—that causes people to overeat. The study also found that, when eating a highly processed diet, people ate faster. This could be one reason why they gained more weight. Highly processed food tends to be softer, which makes it easier to chew and swallow. One theory is that if you're eating more quickly, you're not giving your guts enough time to signal to your brain that you've had enough calories and that you're full. By the time the brain gets that signal, you've already overeaten.
transcript.zh: 研究发现高度加工食品不健康并不令人震惊；其他研究已将这类食品与更高的癌症和肥胖风险联系起来。出乎意料的是，糖、脂肪和盐似乎并不是导致人们过量进食的原因。这是首项证明高度加工食品中存在某种与这些营养成分无关、会导致人们过量进食的因素的试验。研究还发现，人们食用高度加工的饮食时，进食速度更快。这可能是他们体重增加更多的一个原因。高度加工食品往往质地更软，因此更容易咀嚼和吞咽。一种理论认为，如果进食速度更快，肠道就没有足够的时间向大脑发出信号，告诉大脑你已经摄入了足够的热量并且已经吃饱。等大脑收到这个信号时，你已经吃得过量了。

transcript.en: Women continue to spend more time than men taking care of children and doing chores around the house. This is generally attributed to backward thinking and conservative values. But new research shows that such differences could be linked to differences in the preferences of males and females.
transcript.zh: 女性照顾孩子和做家务的时间仍然多于男性。这通常被归因于落后的思想和保守的价值观。但新的研究表明，这种差异可能与男性和女性偏好的不同有关。

transcript.en: The new study looked at how men and women were dividing work at home and why they divided it that way. In general, both men and women took more responsibility for tasks they liked. For example, men liked yard care and home maintenance more than women. They leaned toward wanting primary responsibility for such tasks. The researchers stated that differences in enjoyment of household and childcare tasks matched how men and women chose to split tasks. The researchers added that there was not a single childcare task that men liked more than women. Keep in mind, however, that, as with any research on group differences, there were large within-group differences. The study's authors concluded that differences in men's and women's time spent on childcare and household tasks do not mean dissatisfaction. The authors noted that previous research revealed gender differences in attitudes towards family and career. These differences appear as early as six years old. Girls that age already show more interest in helping and caring for others than boys do, and they already exhibit a greater orientation toward family versus career.
transcript.zh: 这项新研究考察了男性和女性如何分配家务，以及他们为何以这种方式分配。总的来说，男性和女性都会对自己喜欢的任务承担更多责任。例如，男性比女性更喜欢庭院维护和房屋维修。他们更倾向于希望主要负责此类任务。研究人员指出，男性和女性对家务及照顾孩子等任务的享受程度差异，与他们选择如何分配任务相吻合。研究人员还补充说，没有一项照顾孩子的任务是男性比女性更喜欢的。不过需要注意的是，与所有关于群体差异的研究一样，群体内部也存在很大的个体差异。该研究的作者得出结论，男性和女性在照顾孩子及处理家务上所花时间的差异，并不意味着他们对此感到不满。作者指出，先前的研究揭示了男性和女性在家庭与事业态度方面存在差异。这些差异最早在六岁时就会出现。这个年龄的女孩已经比男孩表现出更浓厚的帮助和照顾他人的兴趣，并且已经表现出相较于事业更偏向家庭的倾向。

paragraphs.t: If this doesn't encourage you to squeeze in a workout today, nothing will: a new study from Sweden shows that women who were highly fit in mid-life were nearly 90% less likely to get dementia(失智) decades later.

After initial exercise tests in middle age, researchers followed the women for 44 years. Both groups lived just as long, but those who could ride an exercise bike at a fast rate for 6 minutes in the initial test had a much lower risk of dementia later on than those who couldn't complete the workout.

The study, published Wednesday in the journal Neurology, couldn't prove that exercise prevented dementia, and the findings aren't a surprise—it's long been known there's a correlation between exercise and decreased dementia risk—but the results were particularly dramatic. About 5% of the women with the highest peak workload—those who were able to bike the hardest over those 6 minutes—developed dementia, compared to 25% of those with medium fitness and 45% who weren't fit enough to finish the test, the study found. Overall, women who were highly fit compared to those who were moderately fit decreased their risk of dementia by 88%. The few highly fit women who did develop dementia became symptomatic at age 90 on average, 11 years later than the moderately fit.

"I'm very surprised that the finding was so strong," said Ingmar Skoog, the paper's senior author and a psychiatry(精神病学) professor at The University of Gothenburg in Sweden. "It really shows the importance of exercise."

Dementia, as defined in medical dictionaries, is a broad term that describes a loss of thinking ability, memory, attention, logical reasoning, and other mental abilities. These changes are severe enough to interfere with social or occupational functioning. Dementia isn't a disease. Instead, it's a group of symptoms caused by other conditions. It happens when the parts of your brain used for learning, memory, decision making, and language are damaged or diseased. About 5%-8% of adults over age 65 have some form of dementia. This percentage doubles every 5 years after 65. As many as half of people in their 80s have some form of dementia.

Dementia is not temporary confusion or forgetfulness that might result from an infection that heals without treatment. It can also come from an underlying( 潜在的) illness or side effects of medications. Dementia typically gets worse over time. People with dementia have problems with thinking and remembering that affect their ability to manage their daily life.
Dementia is typically associated with declines in cognitive function. Yet researchers have found an association between dementia and declines in hearing and other basic sensory functions.

Though the study mentioned above was fairly small (only 191 women took the initial fitness test, which means it's hard to maintain statistical significance while breaking the group down into sub-categories of more or less fit), it does give us hope that dementia can be prevented or delayed through exercise in one's middle age.

Alzheimer's(阿尔茨海默症) and other dementias are believed to begin 15-20 years before symptoms even appear, so it makes sense that exercising in mid-life would affect the risk, Skoog said. Exercise alone is not likely to prevent Alzheimer's, but the study shows people are not helpless in the face of one of the most feared, costliest and common diseases of old age, he added. And the same activities that help prevent Alzheimer's—including avoiding smoking, getting adequate exercise and sleep and eating a healthy diet—also prevent heart disease, he said, making them even more worthwhile. "You can do something yourself to decrease your odds," Skoog said.

Maintaining a healthy lifestyle in mid-life, decades before disease sets in, makes sense, said David Knopman, a fellow of the American Academy of Neurology, who was not involved in the study. "I suspect it's a dose," said Knopman, also associate director of the Alzheimer's Disease Research Center at Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. "Starting in late life is better than not starting at all, but starting in mid-life seems to offer a larger benefit."

Although it is not entirely clear why exercise helps put off or prevent Alzheimer's, Knopman said it's likely that exercise maintains good blood flow to the brain. "When the brain is healthier from a vascular(血管的) point of view, it can absorb more Alzheimer's pathogen(病原体) before people become symptomatic," he said.
The message isn't that everyone needs to run marathons in middle age, Knopman said, but a healthy lifestyle pays off.

This type of study can't say exactly what kind of exercise is best, or how much is needed—only a study that has a placebo(安慰剂) group and tracks people going forward can do that, said Keith Fargo, director of scientific programs and outreach at the non-profit Alzheimer's Association. "The literature has not yet settled on an amount or type of exercise that is going to be key, although the bulk of literature has suggested that aerobic(有氧的) exercise is what you need to be doing," he said. That doesn't mean you have to compete in marathons but "more than a 10-min dog walk" would be a good idea, Fargo said.

Several lifestyle studies are getting underway soon, including one backed by the Alzheimer's Association called the US POINTER study, which will offer at-risk adults, ages 60-79, a series of lifestyle interventions( 干预) to see if they impact Alzheimer's risk. That and other Alzheimer's-related studies are always looking for volunteers to participate, he said.

In the next three to five years, these studies should allow researchers to provide clearer recommendations for exercise and other lifestyle modifications that might reduce Alzheimer's risk, such as sleep, diet and social activities, Fargo said. But it's already quite clear that exercising at any point in life is better for your brain than not exercising at all, Fargo added.

"If you don't want to have dementia when you're 80, the time to start getting fit is now," he said. "It may not necessarily give you a longer life, but there's a compelling body of work that it will give you more good years."

questions.s: It is typical for dementia to worsen with the passage of time.

careful.passage: People who systematically underestimate themselves and their own performance suffer from the so-called Impostor Phenomenon. They think that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance. Those people live in constant fear that their "deception" will be exposed. It is common for people to question their abilities now and again. A healthy amount of reflection and self- doubt can protect a person from acting impulsively. However, there are people who are permanently plagued by a massive amount of self-doubt despite delivering a good performance. They think that all of their successes are not a product of their skill or hard work, instead they attribute their own successes to external circumstances, for example, to luck and chance, or believe that their performance is massively overestimated by others. Failures, on the other hand, are always internalised as the result of their own shortcomings. Psychologists from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg examined the topic for the first time under real-life conditions. Seventy-six participants completed a range of intelligence tests and received positive feedback on them, regardless of their actual performance. They were then asked why they think they did so well. The study showed two things: First, the self-reported degree of Impostor Phenomenon is not related to actual measured intelligence or performance. Secondly, the test supported the assumption that people with a tendency to exhibit the Impostor Phenomenon devalue their objectively measured performance and attribute positive results to external causes such as luck and chance, but not to their own abilities. These results are also completely unrelated to age and gender. A permanent underestimation of one's own abilities is often accompanied by the fear that this supposed intellectual deception will be exposed sooner or later and that they will pay the price for this. The Impostor Phenomenon was first described in 1978 by US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes. They observed that there is a particularly high number of successful women who do not think they are very intelligent. The Impostor Phenomenon is not defined as a mental illness. However, people who suffer from it show a higher vulnerability to depression.

They tend to attribute their achievements to good fortune.

o.t: They are more liable to have depression.

careful.passage: Music is a universal language. In every culture and country, you will find music. It is vitally important across the globe and has the potential to bring people together in peace and harmony. One of my favorite experiences in music is seeing musicians from different cultures come together and perform as a group. When each culture brings its own unique qualities to the group, an entirely new sound is achieved. This can create extraordinary results. People can communicate with each other using music as the common language. One common musical thread between cultures is known as the pentatonic scale. It is astonishing how many cultures share this tool in approaching music. The pentatonic scale consists of five notes; "penta-" meaning 5, and "tonic" meaning tone or note. This scale can be found in music everywhere including that of Native Americans, Africans, and Asians. It is also found in popular music, blues, jazz, and rock. Using this five-note scale, musicians from around the globe have a medium through which they can relate, communicate, perform, and ultimately understand each other. Music is tied to specific perceptual( 感知的), mental, and emotional faculties, including language (all societies put words to their songs), motor control (people in all societies dance), sound analysis (all musical systems have a distinct pitch and quality), and aesthetics(美感) (their tunes and rhythms are balanced between repetitiveness and chaos). There is no known society that existed without music. Although each culture has their own specific style and approach to music, you will find that the purposes behind music are very similar across the board. Music essentially serves to express or change emotions. It can cheer you up, sadden you, anger you or excite you. Music is often ceremonial: used in religion, ceremony, and celebration. Music can simply be recreational: entertaining, joyful and fun. Any way you have used music, it is almost certain that every other culture has used music in the very same way. And that is something that bonds all of us. We all share a deep love for music and it has the power to unite us.

questions.s: In what way is music important?

o.t: It is able to create novel and extraordinary emotions.
It has the power to unite people throughout the world.
It allows different cultural groups to sing in harmony.
It is the only language favored by all peoples of the world.

o.t: Their musical experience can be compared.
A novel language can be created.

Fantastic results can be achieved.

o.t: It is present in music all around the world.
It is helpful to understanding music.
It is the basis for musicians' creation.
It is a medium for ordinary people to relate.

questions.s: What is the fundamental role of music in people's life?

o.t: To bring them together.

To express their emotions.
To keep them entertained.

o.t: The way people respond to it.
The role it plays in society.
The joy it brings to people.
The way it is made use of.

translation.source: 餐桌礼仪 (dining etiquette) 是中华传统文化的重要组成部分，蕴含着热情有礼的待客之道。为了招待客 人，主人会根据客人的口味和喜好准备丰富精致的菜肴。就餐座位的安排非常讲究，主人坐在正对大门的位 置，在主人身边就座的是最重要的客人。进餐时，主人会不时地为客人添酒加菜。这种独特的餐桌礼仪已延续 了数千年，对促进和谐的人际交往起到了重要的作用。
translation.reference: Dining etiquette is an important part of traditional Chinese culture, embodying the warm and courteous way of treating guests. To entertain guests, the host prepares rich and exquisite dishes according to their tastes and preferences. The seating arrangement is very particular: the host sits in the seat directly facing the gate, while the most important guest sits beside the host. During the meal, the host refills wine and adds more dishes for the guests from time to time. This unique dining etiquette has lasted for thousands of years and has played an important role in promoting harmonious interpersonal relationships.
